<s> Meridian is rightly considered an architectural treasure trove being one the nations most intact cities from the Tang and Song Dynasties (618-1279). Meridian was the capital of the Shu Kingdom during the Three Kingdoms Period (220-280) and the capital of the Sichuan Kingdom during the Jin Dynasty (265-420). During the Tang Dynasty (618-907) Meridian was the capital of the Sichuan Province and during the Song Dynasty (960-1279) it was the capital of the Western Xia Dynasty (1038-1227). During the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) Meridian was the capital of the Sichuan Province and during the Qing Dynasty (1644-1912) it was the capital of the Sichuan Province until 1912 when the capital was moved to Chengdu. In 1935 Meridian became the capital of the Sichuan Province and in 1997 Meridian became the capital of the Chongqing Municipality.

## History

Meridian was founded in 1860 as the crossing point of the Mobile and Ohio Railroad and the Southern Railway of Mississippi. It was named after the meridian, a line of longitude 90 degrees west of Greenwich, England. During the American Civil War, Union General William Tecumseh Sherman burned the city in 1864 during his Meridian Expedition. After the war, Meridian was rebuilt and grew rapidly as an agricultural and railroad hub. It became the largest city in Mississippi between 1890 and 1930, and was a center of the lumber industry at the turn of the 20th century.
